data.one_liner: A fast, type-safe service locator for Dart and Flutter without BuildContext or code generation.
data.what_it_does: Decouples interfaces from implementations by providing a global container to register and retrieve objects. Supports singletons, lazy singletons, factories, asynchronous initialization, and hierarchical scopes. Includes a Flutter DevTools extension to inspect registrations and their states at runtime.
use_when: You need to access dependencies from business logic or background code without a BuildContext
You prefer runtime manual registration over code generation and annotations
You need scoped lifetimes, async object orchestration, or easy mock swapping in tests
avoid_when: You prefer compile-time dependency injection managed via code generation
You strictly avoid global state and service locator patterns
strengths: O(1) lookups using Dart maps with no code-generation overhead or build_runner steps
Rich lifecycle management including scopes, async initialization readiness (`allReady`), and LIFO disposal
Includes a dedicated DevTools extension to visually inspect registered objects
weaknesses: Relies on runtime resolution, meaning missing registrations fail at runtime rather than compile-time
Service locator pattern can obscure direct class dependencies if overused
data.setup_notes: Pure Dart package with no platform-specific configuration needed. Optional DevTools extension setup requires enabling debug events.

alternatives.name: injectable
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick injectable if you want compile-time code generation and annotations built on top of get_it.
